newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: New crew successfully blasts off for troubled Mir.
newsitem.headline: New crew successfully blasts off for troubled Mir.

text.p: A relief team of two Russian cosmonauts blasted off for the ailing space station Mir at 1536 GMT on Tuesday in a trouble-free launch.

Commander Anatoly Solovyov and flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov were expected to undertake the most vital repairs in the history of the station, which collided with a supply ship on June 25 and is running on partial power. The men were scheduled to arrive on Thursday.
Mission Control outside Moscow broadcast live footage of the cosmonauts, dressed in their spacesuits and strapped into their seats, as they blasted into orbit.
Solovyov waved goodbye as the rocket lifted off, and could later be seen reading from a flight manual.

"The launch went normally, and 526 seconds after lift-off it became clear that the astronauts were in weightlessness when a talisman they had with them for good luck started floating," cosmonaut Viktor Afanasiyev told reporters at Mission Control outside Moscow.
The tall, narrow Proton rocket blasted off in a blaze of yellow light against the darkening evening sky.

The launch at the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan attracted an usually high-ranking Russian delegation, including Defence Minister Igor Sergeyev and Yuri Baturin, secretary of President Boris Yeltsin's Defence Council.
Solovyov, 49, a four-time veteran of the Mir space station, has spent a total of 456 days in space. Vinogradov, 43, is flying for the first time but will lead efforts to repair the ship.
The team is expected to don spacesuits on August 20 to reattach cables to the damaged Spektr module, an operation which, if successful, will restore power to much of the space station.

"We are very glad that this launch has taken place," Valery Kubasov, a cosmonaut on the 1975 Apollo-Soyuz flight, told Reuters. "The cosmonauts have very difficult work ahead. But this launch showed that the crew will complete this work."
